data.hp_running_w: The compressor runs above this many watts
data.hp_standby_w: Standby above this many watts (the compressor stands)

data_description.hp_min_on_s:
Compressor protection: stays ON at least this long.

**When to change it:** When the heat pump's maker gives another run time. **Recommended:** 1200 s (20 min) or more. ⚠ Short compressor runs wear it and lower the COP.
data_description.hp_min_off_s:
Compressor protection: stays OFF at least this long.

**When to change it:** When the heat pump's maker gives another pause. **Recommended:** 600 s (10 min) or more. ⚠ The compressor needs rest between starts.
data_description.hp_standby: Stays ON with the lowest target when nothing is needed (e.g. a unit that protects itself only while ON).
data_description.hp_idle_off: In standby: switches OFF after a long time with no demand.
data_description.hp_idle_hours: After this many hours with no demand.
data_description.hp_running_w: When the "runs" signal is a power meter, above this many W it counts as running (100 W by default).
data_description.hp_standby_w: When the run signal is a power meter: above this but below the compressor's threshold the heat pump is in standby (switched on, for frost protection or circulation for example, but the compressor stands). Below it, it stands. It only makes the display exact; for the coordination standby is "does not run", as before.

data.hp_auto_summer: Automatic summer / winter mode (by the house's demand)
data.hp_summer_after_h: Summer mode after this long without demand
data.hp_winter_after_s: Back to winter when the circuits' demand lasted this long (0 = at once)
data.hp_exercise: Exercise due signal in summer mode (the PLC runs it)

data_description.hp_auto_summer: Not by date: summer mode after a long time with no room demand; back to winter on the circuits' lasting demand.
data_description.hp_summer_after_h: Summer mode after this many hours with no demand.
data_description.hp_winter_after_s: One TPI pulse or airing does not bring the heating back.
data_description.hp_exercise: Signals weekly in summer mode; the PLC runs the pumps.
data_description.hp_exercise_min: How long the signal lasts, in minutes.

data_description.hp_cold_on: Only for a water-filled monoblock: stays ON in frost so the unit's own frost protection can work. It does not replace it.
data_description.hp_cold_release_s: …when it stays above for this long.

data.hp_wood_rise: Tank warming that means another source (°C/h)
data.hp_wood_first: Wood first: also no low-charge start, and a running heating stops (frost protection and cold-weather ON stay)
data.wood_on_above: Wood active when the boiler is at least
data.wood_off_below: Wood inactive when the boiler is at most
data.wood_confirm_s: Lasting this long before it changes

data_description.hp_wood_rise: If the tank warms faster than this while the heat pump does not run, HC takes it as wood burning.
data_description.hp_wood_first: On: no heat pump charging while wood burns (frost and cold-weather ON stay).
data_description.wood_on_above: Wood boiler thermometer above this: burning.
data_description.wood_off_below: …and under this: out. The band between stops flapping.
data_description.wood_confirm_s: It must last this long before it switches.

data.hp_deadband: New target only for a difference of at least
data.hp_max_rise: Rise at most per change (0 = no limit)
data.hp_charge_jump: Full target at once for a new charge

data_description.hp_deadband: No new target for small wobbles.
data_description.hp_confirm_s: The difference must last this long.
data_description.hp_min_interval_s: At least this long between two changes.
data_description.hp_urgent: A difference this large does not wait.
data_description.hp_charge_jump: When a charge starts, and when the compressor stops below the target during a charge, the given-out target goes straight to the worked-out value; the hold only smooths changes within a charge.

data.hp_power_entity: Electric power for the COP (W / kW, optional)
data.hm_heat_min_power_w: Minimum electric power for heat production (W)
data.hm_max_age_s: A reading may be at most this old
data.hm_max_gap_s: No energy over a gap longer than
data.hm_cop_min_s: COP only after this much active running
data.hm_cop_max: A COP above this is implausible

data_description.hp_flow_out_temp_entity: The thermometer of the water leaving the heat pump. The heat meter works only with all three water readings; left empty nothing changes.
data_description.hp_flow_in_temp_entity: The thermometer of the water returning to the heat pump.
data_description.hp_water_flow_entity: Water flow in l/min (L/h and m³/h converted). Heat = l/min × ΔT × 0.06977 kW.
data_description.hp_power_entity: When the “heat pump runs” signal is not a W/kW power (binary, Hz …), give a separate power meter here. Empty: the “runs” signal when it is a power; otherwise no COP, the heat is measured anyway.
data_description.hm_compressor_entity: Compressor frequency (Hz). Preferred for heat metering; stale Hz stops metering, with no silent power fallback. If empty, reuse an Hz running signal or electric power.
data_description.hm_heat_min_power_w: Separate heat-meter production threshold, 200 W by default. Exclude pump-only frost circulation without altering the HP control threshold.
data_description.hm_power_scope: The whole outdoor unit (compressor, fan, pump) or the compressor only – for reading the COP.
data_description.hm_factor: 1.00 for pure water; lower for a glycol mix (30 % glycol ≈ 0.93). An estimate.
data_description.hm_resolution: 1 °C for whole-degree (Tuya) thermometers. With a small ΔT the error is ± resolution / ΔT – the panel shows it.
data_description.hm_min_flow: A smaller flow is 0 kW (circulation stopped).
data_description.hm_max_age_s: A value not reported for longer is stale: counting pauses, no COP.
data_description.hm_max_gap_s: Between two valid readings further apart (an outage, a restart) no energy is added, nothing is filled in.
data_description.hm_cop_window_s: The current COP is the heat of this much active running over its electricity (not a mean of momentary ratios).
data_description.hm_cop_min_s: No COP for this long at the start of a run (thermometers and circulation settle).
data_description.hm_cop_max: A higher value means a wrong reading: not shown.

targets.title: How warm, and when? – {name}
targets.description: Only the targets and the night's times; they apply when saved, every other setting stays.

data_description.target_home:
At home and awake. Also settable from the thermostat card.

**When to change it:** When it is too cool or too warm at home in the day. **Recommended:** 20–22 °C; each degree costs about 6 % heating energy. ⚠ A high target uses a lot and dries the air.
data_description.target_night:
Between the night's start and end (below), and in the Sleep preset.

**When to change it:** When it is cold at night or the morning rise is slow. **Recommended:** 1–3 °C below the home target. ⚠ A deeper setback makes the morning rise longer and harder.
data_description.target_away:
When nobody is home (by the presence entities) or in the Away preset.

**When to change it:** When it is too cold on coming home, or to save more. **Recommended:** 15–18 °C. ⚠ A too low target makes the heat-up after coming home long.
data_description.target_vacation: In the Vacation preset – a short absence keeps the Away target.
data_description.frost_temp:
It never cools below this, not even while off or with a window open.

**When to change it:** Almost never; only for a very cold space (garage, workshop). **Recommended:** 6–8 °C. ⚠ Below 5 °C a pipe behind a colder wall may already freeze.
data_description.night_start: The sleep target applies from this time.
data_description.night_end: The sleep target lasts until this; optimal start times itself to it.
data_description.night_start_weekend: For Friday and Saturday evening's night (ending on Saturday and Sunday morning). Empty: as on weekdays. Give both the start and the end.
data_description.night_end_weekend: On Saturday and Sunday morning the sleep target lasts until this – e.g. 08:00 if you sleep longer at the weekend.

lite.title: HC Lite – the device
lite.description: The address the uploader printed (upload_shelly.py --lite), e.g. http://IP/script/1/lite, its token, and the Shelly's own password if it has one.

data_description.lite_token: Shown once by the uploader; kept on the device (hc_lite_token).
data_description.lite_password: Needed when the Shelly is protected with a password (user admin). With it, the device's own page may change the target too.

lite_settings.title: HC Lite – settings
lite_settings.description: Sent to the device when saved; the device heats by them with or without Home Assistant. A new instance starts in shadow (it decides, the relay is not switched).

data.lite_boost: Boost from this far below the target
data.lite_boost_end: Boost end (this close to the target)
data.lite_sensor_max_age: A reading is too old after

data_description.lite_ctl: Hysteresis: on below target − band/2, off above target + band/2. TPI: demand = base + gain × (target − room), it heats for that share of each cycle. PI: TPI plus an integral that learns the steady need of the house, so a lasting gap closes by itself.
data_description.lite_sensor_id: bthomesensor:ID of the BLU H&T's temperature (Shelly page → Components), or temperature:ID of an add-on probe. Not used with a Wi-Fi H&T (push): its webhook sends the reading to the relay's …/script/1/lite?tok=TOKEN&t=TEMPERATURE (ev.tC on the H&T); set the age limit to 7200 s then, as the H&T sends on a change only.
data_description.lite_shadow: Run it first beside the old thermostat; untick when it may switch the boiler.
data_description.lite_ti: PI only: in how many seconds the integral adds one more step of the gain for a steady 1 °C error. Shorter learns faster but may swing; 14400 s (4 h) suits most houses.
data_description.lite_boost: TPI/PI only: this far or more below the target, it heats without a break (the longest burn still holds). 0: no boost.
data_description.lite_boost_end: The boost lasts until the room is this close to the target; then the cycle takes over.
data_description.lite_pre: The day target starts this much earlier before the day period, for each degree the room is short: e.g. 30 min/°C and 1.5 °C short = 45 minutes early. Once begun, it holds until the day starts. 0: no preheat.
data_description.lite_pre_max: It never starts preheating earlier than this (minutes), however short the room is.
data_description.lite_src: A gas boiler or a heat pump. Only a heat pump can cool (set the heat pump itself to cooling on its own controller; the relay switches the request only).
data_description.lite_hum_id: -1: none (a Wi-Fi H&T sends it itself). A BLU H&T's humidity: bthomesensor 200.., an add-on DHT22: humidity 100..
data_description.lite_dew_id: -1: none. An add-on DS18B20 on the cooled flow pipe (temperature 100..): when the pipe falls below dew point + margin, cooling stops at once. Without one it only warns.
data_description.lite_dew_margin: Cooling stops this far above the dew point (and starts again 1 °C above that).
data_description.lite_buf: Up to 3 add-on probe ids, comma separated, e.g. 100, 101, 102. Shown only; they do not steer anything.
data_description.lite_bufn: Their names, comma separated, e.g. top, middle, bottom (at most 16 characters).
data_description.lite_cf_delta: The comfort preset (and one push of the BLU button) raises the program's target this much (cooling: lowers it).
data_description.lite_cf_time: …for this long, then the program again. Asked again: this much longer (at most 3×).
data_description.lite_btn: -1: none. The bthomedevice:ID of the BLU H&T (or BLU Button) paired to the relay (its button's pushes): one push comfort, two pushes away / back, a long push all back to the program. Works without Home Assistant.
data_description.lite_presence: Everyone away for 20 minutes → away for 12 hours (renewed while away); someone back → the program again, also over a vacation. A person, a group or a sensor with Otthon / Távol (home / away) states.
data_description.lite_calendar: An event whose title has 'szabadság' / 'nyaralás' / 'távol' / 'vacation' → vacation until its end, preheated back on time; 'otthon' / 'home office' → the weekend program that day.
data_description.lite_windows: Any open for 2 minutes → frost protection while open (at most an hour); closed → back at once.

check.title: Why heating / why not? – {name}

sensors.title: Thermometers and windows – {name}
sensors.description: Only the thermometers, the windows and presence; saved at once, every other setting stays. What HC switches (relay, thermostat) is changed under **Another device drives the heating**.{rooms}

data_description.indoor_entity: It regulates by this one. After a new thermometer or a re-pairing, pick it again here.
data_description.outdoor_entity: A weather entity also works. Required for a heating curve; otherwise used for the heat need and the summer rest.
data_description.window_entities: While one is open, the heating pauses.
data_description.presence_entities: A person, a presence sensor or a household state: when nobody is home, the away target applies.

error.confirm_active: Confirm your choice for active mode.
error.humidity_required: Floor cooling needs a humidity sensor (no cooling without a dew point).
error.buffer_order: The stop temperature must be above the start temperature.
error.demand_required: This instance has no room thermometer: the wall thermostat contact is required.
error.climate_taken: This climate is an HC thermostat or is driven by another HC instance already – two would fight over it.
error.cycle_too_short: The cycle is too short for the useful heat delay: at least the delay + the minimum on + the minimum off time (e.g. 20 minutes for a 10-minute delay with 5 + 5).
error.confirm_required: Confirm your choice for a system that is not recommended.
error.indoor_required: Give a room thermometer or a wall thermostat contact.
error.rooms_need_valves: Rooms work with TPI or PID only. Remove them in the Rooms menu first, then change the control.
error.season_order: The heating season's start (the "starts below" value) must be lower than its end.
error.plaus_frost: The lowest believable room temperature can be at most the frost target minus 2 °C.
error.circuit_order: The highest flow target must be above the lowest.
error.cold_order: The release limit must be at or above the ON limit.
error.charge_order: The stop charge must be above the start charge.
error.no_output: Writing needs at least one output entity.
error.wood_order: The off threshold must be below the on threshold.
error.weekend_both: The weekend night needs both a start and an end (or leave both empty).
error.heat_meter_three: The heat meter needs all three water readings (flow, return, water flow) – or none.
error.heat_meter_same: The flow and the return thermometer cannot be the same entity.
error.guard_url: The guard's address must start with http:// or https://.
error.guard_ttl: The lease must be valid at least twice the renewal.
error.guard_token_required: The local guard needs its token (the guard's KVS hc_guard_token).
error.lite_unreachable: The device does not answer at that address
error.not_ready: Not ready to go live yet: at least one blocker is open. The HC info panel's "Ready to go live?" block lists what to fix first (shadow mode keeps calculating meanwhile).
error.outdoor_required: A heating curve needs an outdoor thermometer.

sensor_problem.title: HC – {name}: a sensor or internal problem

source_problem.title: HC – {name}: heat source problem
source_problem.description:
The heat source of **{name}** shows a problem since {since}: **{problem}**.

Check the boiler (error code, gas, flame, relay). HC goes on regulating as well as it can. This entry clears itself as soon as the source is fine. For a notification use the blueprint that comes with HC.

circuit_problem.title: HC – {name}: mixing circuit watch
circuit_problem.description:
The **{name}** mixing circuit, since {since}: **{problem}**.

HC does not act on this, it only reports it. Check the PLC (pump enable, start delay), the mixing valve and its controller (an ESP, for example), and the tank's temperature. The entry clears itself once the circuit works again. The waiting times can be set in the circuit's settings, where the watch can also be switched off.

write_failed.title: HC – {name}: the heat pump does not take HC's value
write_failed.description:
**{entity}** shows {value} instead of the {want} HC asks for, and {tries} restores did not help. HC stops writing it until the value it wants changes or the unit shows HC's value again.

Check the unit: its mode (off / auto / manual), its app or controller (Tuya, a local integration), and whether something else writes it. The entry clears itself once the unit follows HC again.

guard_problem.title: HC – {name}: local guard
guard_problem.description:
The local guard of **{name}** ({url}) {problem}.

Check the guard device and the network. This entry clears itself once HC controls normally again.

safety_stop.title: HC – LIFE-SAFETY STOP
safety_stop.description:
Alarm from: **{by}**.

HC stopped all heating and keeps it stopped. When the danger is over and every detector is clear, press **Acknowledge the life-safety stop**. The wired chain (gas valve, contactor, water valve) is reset on site by its own button.

safety_input_lost.title: HC – a life-safety input has no reading
safety_input_lost.description: **{inputs}** has had no reading for 10 minutes. While it has none it cannot trip HC's life-safety stop (the wired safety chain still can). Check the detector (battery, connection). This entry clears itself when it reports again.

trv_no_heads.title: HC – {name}: no TRV head
trv_no_heads.description:
**{name}** is set to *TRV heads only*, but none of its rooms has a TRV head – it sets nothing.

Add the rooms with their heads: Settings → Devices & services → HC Thermostat → Configure → Rooms (or run the HC setup wizard again). Put each head's device in its room's area. This entry clears itself once a room has a head.

lite_comfort.name: HC Lite comfort
lite_comfort.description: The program's target plus the comfort step, for the comfort time (again: longer). The relay ends it by itself.

lite_vacation.name: HC Lite vacation
lite_vacation.description: Away until the given time; the relay preheats so it is warm on arrival, then follows its program.
